extra.claim: A caller can disable the required overdue email through the new config option, which no requirement asks for.
extra.why: src/jobs/nightly.js:11 takes a config param and src/notifications/NotificationService.js:16-19 returns without sending when the event is disabled, so {events:{"invoice.overdue":{enabled:false}}} silently delivers nothing; the brief specifies no opt-out.

extra.claim: The new output test never goes through loadInvoices, so combining service and archive invoices is untested end to end.
extra.why: test/outputs.test.js:9 builds invoices by calling readArchive directly, while src/invoices/load.js:5-6 is the entry that combines fetchInvoices and readArchive; no test exercises that combination, so a loader regression would pass.

extra.claim: The refused-send test checks only counters and the next night's sends, never the content of the refused night's deliveries, so a regression mis-addressing the other customer would pass.
extra.why: test/nightly.test.js:38-45 asserts {sent:1,failed:1} and the next night's recipients but never inspects refusing.sent, so a wrong-address send marked successful passes.

extra.claim: No test distinguishes UTC from another calendar zone, so a regression deriving today from local time would pass the suite.
extra.why: Every test night in test/nightly.test.js:6 is 01:00:00Z, which maps to the same calendar date in e.g. UTC+3, so a local-date regression yields the same outcomes though it could notify before midnight UTC.

extra.claim: A quoted field holding a line break is split into separate rows, so a valid CSV name spanning lines is never imported as one contact.
extra.why: src/contacts/import.js:13 splits the text on \n before quote handling, so a quoted name containing a newline becomes two broken rows; parseCsv in src/lib/csv.js supports embedded line breaks and record line numbers.

extra.claim: A quoted field holding a line break is split into separate rows, corrupting data and rejected-row line numbers.
extra.why: src/contacts/import.js:13 splits on \n before interpreting quotes, so a quoted name containing a newline is treated as several records; parseCsv in src/lib/csv.js handles such fields.

extra.claim: The page's try/catch substitutes a fabricated USD 0.00 price for errors no supported invoice can produce, masking real failures.
extra.why: src/screens/page.js:5-9 catches and returns 'USD 0.00'; node_modules/@acme/billing-client/index.js:11,14 and data/archive.schema.json guarantee a string currency and an integer amount, so nothing inside the try throws under supported inputs.

extra.claim: Duplicate counting is tested only against the plan, not through importContacts, so a counting regression in the public entry point would pass.
extra.why: test/import.test.js:15-21 checks a repeated email only via planImport while the importContacts test at lines 23-30 uses distinct emails, so a double-counting regression in importContacts passes.

extra.claim: A valid quoted field containing a newline is split into separate rows.
extra.why: src/contacts/import.js:13 splits into physical lines and toggles quotes per line, so a quoted name holding a line break is broken into several records; src/lib/csv.js:16-30 handles multiline fields and record lines.

extra.claim: Duplicate counts are not tested through importContacts, so an import that processes duplicate rows separately could pass the suite.
extra.why: test/import.test.js:15-21 covers a repeated new email only through planImport; the importContacts test at lines 23-30 uses distinct emails, so a double-counting regression passes.

extra.claim: The page's catch replaces any exception with a fabricated USD 0.00 price, though supported sources provide a currency string and integer amount that cannot throw on the formatting path.
extra.why: src/screens/page.js:5-9 swaps any error for 'USD 0.00'; node_modules/@acme/billing-client/index.js:11,14 and data/archive.schema.json guarantee a string currency and integer amount, so the try's operations cannot throw for supported invoices.
